items.prompt: White to move (Deep Blue, game 6). If the knight on g5 takes the pawn on e6, how many black pieces can take it back?

claims.statement: After Nxe6, one black piece can capture the knight on e6.
The black pawn on f7 is that piece.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Nxe6.

hints: Look at which black pieces attack e6 right now.
Count attackers of the square e6 once the knight is on it.
Not a piece: one of the pawns.
items.explain: Exactly one black piece, the pawn on f7, can take the knight on e6. At depth 16 the engine also ranks the capture first. Depth-limited evidence, not proof.

items.prompt: White to move. If the bishop goes to g6, how many black pieces can capture it there?

claims.statement: After Bg6+, no black piece attacks the bishop on g6.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bg6+.
The black king stands on e8.

hints: Check each black piece in turn: which squares does it attack?
Does any black pawn or piece cover g6?
Also ask what the bishop on g6 attacks.
items.explain: No black piece covers g6, so the bishop checks the king without being taken; the king must move and loses its right to castle. At depth 16 the engine ranks the check first.

items.prompt: Black to move (game 2). Find the move the engine ranks first.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Qe3.
At depth 16 Qxc6 is at least 2 pawns below Qe3.
The white king stands on f1.

hints: Look at White's king on f1 and the queen on b6.
Which black move brings the queen closer to that king?
The queen goes to the third rank.
items.explain: At depth 16 the engine puts the queen move to e3 first and the queen trade on c6 far behind. Whether it holds a draw is the open question of this lesson.

feedback_by_move.b6c6: Trading queens. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 2 pawns below Qe3.

items.prompt: Black to move: White has a bishop and a rook pawn against a bare king. With best play, who wins?

claims.statement: The 7-man tablebase says the position (Black to move) is a draw.
At depth 16 the engine rates it slightly better for White (about +0.7), not a draw: a score is not the result.
A white bishop stands on f1 (a light square).
A white pawn stands on h6.

hints: Look at the corner h8 where Black's king stands.
Which squares can this bishop ever reach from f1?
items.explain: The bishop and the promotion corner h8 are on opposite colours, so the bishop can never drive the king from the corner: a draw by the tablebase, though the depth-16 engine score is slightly above level.

items.prompt: Black to move: White has a bishop and a rook pawn against a bare king. With best play, who wins?

claims.statement: The 7-man tablebase says Black, the side to move, loses.
A white bishop stands on g1 (a dark square).
A white pawn stands on h6.

hints: Look at the corner h8 where Black's king stands.
Which squares can this bishop ever reach from g1?
items.explain: Now the bishop is on the same colour as the corner h8, so it can control the queening square: a win by the tablebase.
